source.title: Feature learning in neural networks and kernel machines that recursively learn features
source.authors: Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan; Daniel Beaglehole; Parthe Pandit; Mikhail Belkin

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a neural network's test accuracy as training continues after it has nearly fit the training data. This bears on the late-training portion of V2, but it does not measure the full fall-rise-fall curve.
record.gate_note: The modified STL-10 experiment reports test accuracy changing during extended training. Other results about feature learning, pruning, and RFM performance do not measure the claim's model-size, sample-size, or full epoch-wise double-descent curves. No test-error sweeps over model size or training-set size are reported.
record.test_reason: The paper is about feature learning via the average gradient outer product. It never measures or mentions double descent, and cites neither original source. Its only time-course result is a grokking demonstration on a deliberately constructed STL-10 subset. Test accuracy sits near 80% after the training set is fit, then rises to 99.38%. No rise in test error is shown, so it is not a fall-rise-fall epoch-wise curve. It also sweeps no model size or sample size. The grokking result is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version. The enum has no 'unrelated' option; cites_only is the nearest fit, although the paper does not actually cite the double-descent literature.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors present the modified STL-10 result as grokking: a network fits the training data without feature learning, with test accuracy around 80%. Continued training learns the star-pattern features and raises test accuracy to 99.38%, which they say aligns with the Deep Neural Feature Ansatz. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: It reports a late-training accuracy change on a modified image task, rather than a full epoch-wise double-descent curve or a sweep around an interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-hidden-layer fully connected ReLU network on modified STL-10 reaches near 100% training accuracy with test accuracy around 80%. Continued training then raises test accuracy to 99.38% as the first-layer feature matrix up-weights the star pixels. An RFM on the same data goes from 55.8% to 100% test accuracy over iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking: delayed generalization after fitting the training set, attributed to late feature learning (not double descent).

record.problems: The relevant temporal result is a single modified-dataset experiment and reports only the late improvement after near-perfect training accuracy, not the full curve. No uncertainty estimate or control for this result is stated.

untested.parts: No sweep of test error over model size.
No epoch-wise test-error curve with a rise; only a grokking-style plateau then improvement.
No sweep over sample size near interpolation.
No capacity sweep across model classes. RFM iterations raise test accuracy, but this is not a capacity axis.
No effective-complexity measure predicting a peak location.
No variation of label noise or regularization in relation to a peak. The RFM ridge term is used only to slow training for visualisation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabelled grokking as the tail of epoch-wise double descent. The paper reports no rise in test error at any point. Mikhail Belkin, an author of the original source arXiv:1812.11118, is a co-author here, but this paper is not an original source for the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep across model sizes or interpolation threshold.
Reports only the late-training improvement after near-perfect training accuracy; it does not establish the full test-error fall-rise-fall shape.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent curves across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across axes.
No test of whether noise or regularization drives, splits, or removes a double-descent peak.
No comparison of double descent with a curve measured against effective parameter count.

rows.subject: two-hidden-layer fully connected network
rows.operation_detail: Measured test accuracy as training continued beyond the point of near-100% training accuracy.

conditions.value: modified STL-10; 553 total training and validation examples, with 500 airplanes and 53 trucks
Adam, learning rate 10^-4, batch size equal to dataset size

rows.baseline: 80% test accuracy after the network reached near-100% training accuracy
rows.note: The authors describe a sharp late-training test-accuracy increase after near-perfect training accuracy. This shows the late improvement portion of the expected epoch-wise curve, but not the preceding decline and rise in test error.
rows.check: This measures grokking: a plateau at about 80% test accuracy, then a rise to 99.38%. Nothing marks a test-error peak near interpolation. The text reports no rise in test error and no early descent, so the measure cannot show V2's fall-rise-fall shape. The setup was also engineered to produce grokking: a star-pattern shortcut, a 500/53 class imbalance and a tiny dataset. The 'partial' state and the V2 link should be removed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
